findings.title: Translation cache key ignores fallback locales, causing stale/wrong cached translations
findings.body: I18n.translate caches results under a key of "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}". With fallbacks enabled, the result of a translation now also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (e.g. translating key X in locale :es may return the :es string, or fall back to the site default locale's or English string). Because the cache key only contains the requested locale, a cached fallback result will be reused even after the site's default_locale changes (or, on a multi-process deployment where the cache lives per process, results computed under an old default_locale persist until the cache is evicted or the process restarts). Users would see translations from the wrong locale until restart. The cache key should include the fallback chain (e.g. I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].join) or the cache must be cleared when default_locale changes.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [], making it a broken/unused Hash
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but its `[]` ignores all hash state and always computes [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. Any other Hash behavior (each, key?, merge, dup, defaults handling in i18n's Fallbacks code) will not see any entries and will behave as an empty hash. i18n-gem code that manipulates the fallbacks object as a hash (e.g. I18n.fallbacks.merge!, inspecting it, or copying it) will silently do nothing or produce wrong results. Either use a plain object that duck-types `[]`/`ensure_loaded!` without the Hash superclass, or actually store the computed fallback chain in the hash so Hash semantics stay consistent.

findings.title: Fallback list can contain the literal symbol of an invalid locale and mixes string/symbol locales
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` assumes SiteSetting.default_locale is always a symbolizable valid locale; if it is ever nil or an unsupported value, `nil.to_sym` raises NoMethodError inside every I18n lookup via the fallback chain, breaking all translations for the request. Additionally, `locale` may be a string or symbol depending on caller (I18n.locale vs raw keys), and `uniq` on mixed types ("de" vs :de) will not deduplicate, potentially causing the same locale to be tried twice per lookup. Normalize all entries with to_sym before uniq and guard against nil.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! only runs for web requests; fallback locales are never loaded in jobs/mailers
findings.body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, and any other entry point that sets I18n.locale (e.g. Discourse's job locale handling, I18n.locale = user locale) will use the fallback chain without the fallback locales being loaded into the backend. Because translate_accelerator forces explicit loading (load_translations ignores empty args) and only loads config.locale inside translate, lookups for the fallback locales (site default locale, or :en) will miss and silently return the next fallback — meaning users get English strings instead of the site-default-locale translations in emails and scheduled jobs. The ensure_loaded! should be invoked wherever I18n.locale is set outside controllers, or translate should load all fallback locales.
